title: Jacobians of abelian Cayley digraphs: an answer to Reiner's question
statement: Let A be a finite abelian group of order n >= 2 and S a multiset of nonzero elements of A with sum 0 that generates A. Then the Jacobian of the Cayley digraph Cay(A, S) is isomorphic to A if and only if A is cyclic and S = {a, -a} for a generator a. More precisely |Jac| > n whenever A is noncyclic or |S| >= 3; if A is cyclic and |S| >= 3 then |Jac| >= (3/2)^phi(n) n, and if the p-part of A is noncyclic then p^(2 + v_p(n)) divides |Jac|. This answers V. Reiner's question (BIRS sandpile-group workshop, problem 1.9) in the affirmative.
resolves: BIRS sandpile-group open problem 1.9 (V. Reiner), 'only if' direction, for finite abelian groups (written argument, pending specialist review; possibly already answered by Benkart-Klivans-Reiner Proposition 6.19, see review/PRIOR_ART.md)
verified: check_cayley_jacobian.py: exhaustive Smith-normal-form check for |A| <= 12, |S| <= 4; product formula n|Jac| = prod lambda_chi; exact orbit-norm factorisation, p^2 divisibility and the AM-GM bound on cyclic groups n <= 12; cyclic-subgroup count exceeding the exponent for noncyclic p-groups of order <= 64; control without the sum-zero hypothesis.
cayley_jac.py: exhaustive scans (|A| <= 24, |S| <= 5: 32,551 cases; |A| <= 14, |S| <= 7: 19,633 cases): Jac ~= A only for cyclic {a, -a}.
check_bound.py (6,236 cases) and check_norms.py (1,601 cyclic cases, exact resultants): all proof ingredients hold.
